articles.title: Paper to Portfolio: a local Gemma reads the old share certificate in your drawer, but never does the maths
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady Lots of Indian families have a drawer with a few old share certificates in it: thick, cream-coloured paper,…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built Lots of Indian families have a drawer with a few old share certificates in it: thick, cream-coloured paper, a company seal, "100 Equity Shares of Rs. 10/- each" , dated sometime in the 1980s. Nobody knows what they are worth. The company on the paper usually no longer exists under that name. Since then there have been bonus issues, a stock split, maybe a merger. And if the dividends went unclaimed for seven years in a row, the shares may have been moved to the government's Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF). Working that out today means weeks of digging through exchange filings, or paying a share-recovery firm.
articles.author: Rahul Kumar

articles.excerpt: Thirty Days From Exposure Census to Verified Remediation: A CVE-2026-102764 Plan CISA set a remediation due date of 2026-10-19 for CVE-2026-102764 under BOD 26-04, and required forensic triage alongsi…
articles.body: Thirty Days From Exposure Census to Verified Remediation: A CVE-2026-102764 Plan CISA set a remediation due date of 2026-10-19 for CVE-2026-102764 under BOD 26-04, and required forensic triage alongside it. Binding or not, the schedule that directive implies works as a template: a month is enough time to go from not knowing what is exposed to being able to evidence remediation. Days 1 to 5: establish the list Run the exposure query against owned address space, certificate subject names and hostname patterns, and record the collection time for every result. Then reconcile the answer against the asset register. ZoomEye reported 2,185 assets matching app="Bomgar" globally on 2026-10-26; the organisation-specific number will be smaller and is the one that governs the plan.

articles.title: AI Needs Better Batteries. Better Batteries Need AI
articles.excerpt: From iron-air batteries to CO₂ storage, the next energy breakthrough may be coordinating electricity and computation—not just inventing a better battery Training a model is a computing problem. Keepin…
articles.body: From iron-air batteries to CO₂ storage, the next energy breakthrough may be coordinating electricity and computation—not just inventing a better battery Training a model is a computing problem. Keeping its infrastructure powered through a windless night, a demand spike, or several days of weak renewable generation is an energy problem. Increasingly, those two problems belong in the same architecture. AI can help improve how energy storage is designed and operated. Energy storage can help supply the electricity that AI infrastructure needs. Between them sits a third opportunity: software that coordinates when electricity is stored, when it is released, and when flexible computation runs. The most interesting connection is not an LLM attached to a battery dashboard. It is coordination .
articles.author: Seyed Alireza Alhosseini

articles.title: Two Roads, One Plan View: Modeling Seattle's SR 99 Tunnel in 3D
articles.excerpt: The first version of my SR 99 model looked fine from above and wrong from everywhere else. I traced the footprint from a map, extruded it, and called it done. Then I cut a section through the middle a…
articles.body: The first version of my SR 99 model looked fine from above and wrong from everywhere else. I traced the footprint from a map, extruded it, and called it done. Then I cut a section through the middle and found one road where there should have been two. The plan view had folded the upper and lower decks into a single line, and my model had believed it. Then the project got interesting. A plan view cannot hold a stack Most map data describes the ground in two dimensions. A road is a line, a building is a polygon, a tunnel is a corridor. That works until the corridor carries traffic on two levels. Under downtown Seattle, both directions share the same coordinates and differ only in elevation. A flat file has nowhere to put that. The fix is simple but deliberate.
articles.author: GenAnywhere

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 25, 1671: Astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovers Iapetus, Saturn's 'yin-yang' moon
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Iapetus was the second moon anyone had ever found orbiting Saturn, and it was the first of four moons Cassini would discover at the ringed planet. The Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens had discovered Titan , the largest of Saturn's moons, about six years earlier. After Cassini found Iapetus, he also found the moons Rhea, Tethys and Dione. When Cassini first saw Iapetus, the moon looked like a tiny speck on the west side of Saturn. He calculated its orbit and thought he would be able to see it again on the east side of Saturn 39 days later, but it was nowhere to be seen.

articles.title: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
articles.excerpt: On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad - whether it's…
articles.body: On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad - whether it's a still image, video, audio, or text - that "has been significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence" to include a label in the same format as the ad itself. That applies to TV commercials from multi-billion-dollar companies , as well as restaurants' ugly, crowded flyers about their wing specials. Pennsylvania is one of the first states to require disclosures on AI content. And it requires those labels regardless of where an ad … Read the full story at The Verge.

articles.body: On Episode 233 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and guest host Rick Jenet are joined by Dr. Amanda Smith-Hackler, the Director of Education for the Universities Space Research Association and Principal Investigator for the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Scholars and STEM Workforce Development Programs, about the new and exciting opportunities available to young people seeking to enter the space workforce.
